const path = "/Volumes/aro/projects/prose_generation/enrichment/bible/work/s001/discovery/pilot1-20261005/1_3/luna/followup.tsv";
const content = `strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Exod.34.7\tforgiveness and accountability\tThe commentary holds mercy beside the judgment day; the next verse after Exodus's mercy formula says God forgives wrongdoing yet does not simply acquit guilt, making the balance explicit.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Exod.22.26\tcompassion protects a debtor\tThe commentary says mercy must reach the vulnerable as a concrete good; the law protects a poor neighbor's pledged cloak and grounds the rule in God's compassionate character.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Gen.21.17\tGod hears the endangered boy\tThe commentary's B003 centers care for a child who cannot yet ask; in the wilderness God hears Ishmael's voice and tells Hagar not to fear, directing care to an abandoned child.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Gen.21.19\twater found for Hagar and Ishmael\tThe commentary describes provision that sustains a child before he can provide for himself; God opens Hagar's eyes to a well, turning rescue into water for mother and child.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Exod.2.6\tcompassion for an exposed infant\tThe commentary's B001 says tenderness should become good for its recipient; Pharaoh's daughter pities the exposed infant Moses and takes steps to preserve him.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:2Sam.9.7\tkindness to a vulnerable kinsman\tThe commentary joins mercy to kinship and active provision; David restores land to disabled Mephibosheth and gives him a place at the royal table for Jonathan's sake.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Deut.32.11\teagle guarding its young\tThe commentary's B003 pictures the womb as protection and nurture; Moses' song compares God's care for Israel to an eagle spreading its wings and carrying its young.
strong\ttevrat\tsoydas\tWLC:Ps.72.13\tHebrew ירחם for the weak\tThe commentary labels Arabic ر ح م as its source root; Psalm 72 uses the Hebrew cognate ירחם for pity on the weak and needy, then says the king saves their lives.
strong\ttevrat\tsoydas\tWLC:Ps.78.38\tcompassion repeatedly restrains anger\tThe commentary balances mercy with judgment; the psalm uses Hebrew רחום as God forgives Israel's wilderness sins, does not destroy them, and repeatedly turns anger aside.
strong\ttevrat\tsoydas\tWLC:Ps.77.9\tcompassions questioned in anger\tThe commentary describes mercy as an enduring quality; the lament uses Hebrew רחמים while asking whether anger has closed off God's compassion, voicing the fear that mercy has ceased.
strong\ttevrat\tsoydas\tWLC:Ps.40.11\tcompassions asked to preserve\tThe commentary labels Arabic ر ح م as its source root; the psalm uses Hebrew רחמים in a plea that God's compassion and faithfulness preserve the speaker from surrounding troubles.
strong\ttevrat\tsoydas\tWLC:Ps.25.6\tancient compassions remembered\tThe commentary places mercy before requests for help; the psalm asks God to remember his Hebrew רחמים and covenant love amid a prayer for direction and forgiveness.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Ps.71.6\ttrust from the mother's womb\tThe commentary's B003 describes the womb as provision before a child can ask; the psalmist says God has sustained him from the womb and has been his praise since birth.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Ps.103.14\thuman frailty remembered\tThe commentary singles out mercy for the weak; the psalm says God remembers that humans are dust and knows their frame, giving compassion a reason grounded in creaturely fragility.
strong\ttevrat\tsoydas\tWLC:Ps.116.5\tHebrew מרחם\tThe commentary labels Arabic ر ح م as its source root; the psalm calls God compassionate with a Hebrew form from the cognate root while also naming him gracious and righteous.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Ps.116.6\trescue of the simple\tThe commentary describes mercy as an act that reaches a recipient; the next verse says the Lord preserves the simple and saves the speaker when brought low.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Prov.19.17\tkindness to the poor as a loan\tThe commentary defines mercy as tenderness that entails practical good; Proverbs says giving to the poor is like lending to the Lord, who repays the deed.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Isa.46.3\tcarried from the womb\tThe commentary's B003 treats the womb as a place of protection; Isaiah depicts God carrying Israel from birth and from the womb, extending the image from an individual child to a people.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Isa.46.4\tcare through old age\tThe commentary distinguishes an enduring quality from a momentary gift; Isaiah says God will carry and deliver his people even into old age, completing the womb-to-lifespan image.
strong\ttevrat\tsoydas\tWLC:Isa.63.15\tcompassions sought in prayer\tThe commentary labels Arabic ر ح م as its source root; Isaiah's prayer uses Hebrew רחמים while asking where God's compassion and zeal have gone, in a plea for renewed aid.
strong\ttevrat\tsoydas\tWLC:Jer.12.15\tcompassion after uprooting\tThe commentary labels Arabic ر ح م; Jeremiah uses the Hebrew cognate as God promises to have compassion on nations after uprooting them and to bring them back.
strong\ttevrat\tsoydas\tWLC:Lam.3.32\tcompassion after grief\tThe commentary says a harsh first appearance may conceal eventual good; Lamentations uses the Hebrew רחם root to say that after causing grief God will show compassion according to abundant love.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Lam.3.33\tGod does not afflict willingly\tThe commentary says mercy's real face appears in the good ultimately delivered; Lamentations says God does not afflict or grieve people from his heart, interpreting suffering without making harm his delight.
strong\ttevrat\tsoydas\tWLC:Hab.3.2\tmercy remembered in wrath\tThe commentary joins compassion to judgment; Habakkuk uses Hebrew רחם in asking God to remember mercy in the midst of wrath.
strong\ttevrat\tsoydas\tWLC:Zech.1.16\tcompassion on Jerusalem restored\tThe commentary labels Arabic ر ح م as its source root; Zechariah uses Hebrew רחמים when God says he has returned to Jerusalem with compassion after the city's desolation.
strong\ttevrat\tsoydas\tWLC:Ezek.39.25\tcompassion in restoration\tThe commentary labels Arabic ر ح م; Ezekiel uses the Hebrew cognate as God promises to restore Jacob and have compassion on all Israel after judgment and exile.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:2Chr.30.9\treturn welcomed by a merciful God\tThe commentary says mercy is named before the worshiper's request; Hezekiah urges the northern Israelites to return for Passover because their God is gracious and compassionate and will not turn away from them.
strong\ttevrat\tsoydas\tWLC:Dan.9.9\tcompassions despite rebellion\tThe commentary labels Arabic ر ح م as its source root; Daniel's Hebrew prayer says compassion and forgiveness belong to God even though the people rebelled.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWisdom of Solomon 12:19\tlenience teaches humaneness\tThe commentary defines mercy as an effective good; Wisdom says God's lenience teaches the righteous to be humane and gives sinners hope of repentance after wrongdoing.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\t2 Maccabees 6:12-16\tdiscipline as correction, not destruction\tThe commentary says a severe-looking act may conceal a beneficial purpose; the author interprets Israel's persecution as discipline that corrects the people rather than a wish to destroy them.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tTobit 4:7-11\talmsgiving for the needy\tThe commentary says mercy must become a deed for its recipient; Tobit instructs his son to give to the poor and links that aid with deliverance from death and cleansing from sin.
strong\ttevrat\tyorum_gelenegi\tMishnah Yoma 8:9\tatonement as a Father's cleansing\tThe commentary holds mercy beside the day of judgment; Rabbi Akiva's closing teaching pictures Israel's purification as a Father cleansing his children, interpreting atonement through filial care.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Luke.1.57\tbirth after a barren season\tThe commentary's B003 develops the womb as a protected place where a child is formed; Luke reports Elizabeth's promised child being born, the event the next verse names as mercy.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Luke.1.58\tbirth recognized as mercy\tThe commentary links the root family with womb and kinship; Elizabeth's neighbors call the Lord's action toward her great mercy after the birth and rejoice with her.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Luke.6.35\tkindness to the ungrateful\tThe commentary presents Rahman as mercy extending broadly; Jesus says God is kind even to the ungrateful and evil, then commands love and practical good toward enemies.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Luke.7.13\tcompassion for a bereaved widow\tThe commentary directs mercy toward the weak; Jesus sees a widow in grief, is moved with compassion, and addresses her, locating divine aid in attention to an exposed and mourning person.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Luke.7.15\ta son restored to his mother\tThe commentary joins compassion to the good it delivers and to kinship; after Jesus' compassion in verse 13, this verse says the son lives and is given back to his mother.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Matt.9.36\tcompassion for a shepherdless crowd\tThe commentary describes mercy as directed to those in need; Jesus sees crowds as harassed and helpless like sheep without a shepherd and responds with compassion.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Rom.2.4\tkindness leads to repentance\tThe commentary describes mercy as nurture that brings a recipient toward completion; Paul says God's kindness, forbearance, and patience are meant to lead the sinner to repentance.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Rom.9.24\tcalled from Jews and Gentiles\tThe commentary distinguishes mercy that encompasses all from mercy directed to particular people; Paul says God's called community includes both Jews and Gentiles.
strong\tincil\tyorum_gelenegi\tSBLGNT:Rom.9.25\tHosea's restoration oracle reapplied\tThe commentary notes that rejected recipients may again receive mercy; Paul quotes Hosea's reversal of not-my-people language for the people God is now calling.
strong\tincil\tyorum_gelenegi\tSBLGNT:1Pet.2.10\tnot shown mercy, now shown mercy\tThe commentary links Rahim to mercy directed toward recipients; Peter applies Hosea's name reversal to a Christian community that was formerly outside mercy and now receives it.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:2Pet.3.9\tpatience delays judgment for repentance\tThe commentary holds mercy and the day of judgment together; Peter says the Lord's patience gives people time to repent rather than perish.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:James.5.11\tcompassion at the end of Job's trial\tThe commentary says mercy may be hidden beneath painful events; James points to Job's endurance and outcome, then names the Lord compassionate and merciful.
strong\tincil\tsoydas\tPeshitta, Luke 7:13\tSyriac rḥm for compassion\tThe commentary labels Arabic ر ح م as its source root; the Peshitta uses the Syriac cognate rḥm for Jesus' compassion toward the bereaved widow.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Titus.3.5\tsalvation through mercy and rebirth\tThe commentary's B003 associates the root family with womb and nurture; Titus says God saves according to mercy through washing and rebirth, not through human works.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Eph.4.32\tcompassion becomes forgiveness\tThe commentary says inward tenderness should issue in good for others; Ephesians tells believers to be compassionate and forgiving as God forgave them in Christ.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:1Tim.1.16\tmercy as a pattern for others\tThe commentary describes mercy reaching particular recipients; Paul says mercy was shown to him so Christ's patience could become an example for later believers.
medium\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:1Thess.2.7\tnursing mother as pastoral image\tThe commentary's B003 develops a womb that protects and nourishes; Paul compares his care for the community to a nursing mother cherishing her children.
medium\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Gal.4.19\tlabor pains until formation\tThe commentary describes a womb that carries a child through stages toward maturity; Paul uses labor pains for his continuing work until Christ is formed in the Galatians.
`;
const r = await tools.exec_command({
  cmd: `cat > '${path}' <<'EOF'\n${content}EOF`,
  max_output_tokens: 100
});
text(r.output);
